decisions.decision: The tool assigns sources, labels and statuses; a model proposes content only

decisions.decision: Verdict policy: a single run never raises a status. SUPPORTED requires model coverage 'full' and every part covered by a structural fact, and two independent runs agreeing (or a person). PARTIAL / PROSE_ONLY / IMPLEMENTED_BY attach evidence only; CONTRADICTED goes to review
decisions.rationale: round 6: part-based coverage alone overclaimed 4 times; two-run agreement had 1 wrong of 7

decisions.decision: Test evidence: link tests to prerequisites (verifies / exercises / unrelated), run each at the commit with --locked, the features its cfg requires, and --exact; import results with from_csv as measured data units; backs / rebuts for verifies, x.code/exercises for exercises. Prerequisite statuses never change from test results alone
decisions.rationale: test-evidence run: 53 tests, 50 passed, attested stores; S1: 3 of 17 'verifies' links wrong, 1 vacuous test
decisions.quote: Test evidence: link tests to prerequisites (verifies / exercises / unrelated), run each at the commit with --locked, the features its cfg requires, and --exact; import results with from_csv as measured data units; backs / rebuts for verifies, x.code/exercises for exercises. Prerequisite statuses never change from test results alone

decisions.decision: The model is the operator's choice, never the tool's
decisions.rationale: Provider (ollama, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), model, endpoint, key variable, context window and the system prompt come from flags, the environment or configuration, with sensible defaults and the prompt tunable per provider; a run records which it used. The default is local (Ollama), so the tool costs nothing to try
decisions.quote: The model is the operator's choice, never the tool's.

decisions.decision: The model client is our own, and the default build has no network stack
decisions.rationale: `check` speaks plain HTTP/1.1 to a local provider (Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint on `http://`), written out rather than pulled in; a hosted provider over TLS is the `hosted` feature, off by default. This settles item 7: smysl's `model` feature would bring `smysl-provider` and a TLS stack into every install, and the multi-pass schemas do not fit `PromptOverride` anyway. `check` ships advisory — findings print, the exit code stays 0 unless `--strict`, which exits 5
decisions.quote: The model client is our own, and the default build has no network stack.

pub const SYSTEM: &str = "You check one claim about a Rust codebase against facts taken from the code.
\
The facts are `F1`, `F2`, … (what the code does) and `P1`, `P2`, … (what the code says about itself: doc comments, string literals, string constants).
\
Break the claim into its parts — each thing it asserts — and for each part say whether the facts show it. Cite the facts you used by name.
\
Rules you must follow:
- Cite only facts you were shown. Do not recall anything about this project from memory.
- A part no fact shows is uncovered. Saying so is the useful answer; guessing is not.
- If a fact shows the claim is false, set `contradicted` and cite it.
- `P` facts are what someone wrote, not what the code does: they may point at the right place, and they never establish a part on their own.
\
Return one JSON object: {"covered": [{"part": string, "facts": [string]}], "uncovered": [string], "contradicted": boolean, "contradicted_by": [string]}";
